description: This walk takes you from Bouley Bay to Rozel on the northern coast of Jersey. The route follows a section of the Jersey Coast Path for a distance of 3.6km. The hike along Jersey's rugged northern coast offers spectacular views over the island's tallest cliffs, which stand at roughly 400 feet. The route follows a "roller-coaster" cliff path that undulates between high-reaching headlands and secluded bays, typically taking about 90 minutes to complete at a steady pace. Starting from the pebble beach at Bouley Bay—a historic haven for smugglers—the trail leads past the mid-19th-century L'Etacquerel Fort, a coastal fortification now available as a unique holiday rental. As you progress toward Rozel, the path winds through wooded gullies and open common ground, providing sweeping vistas of small fishing harbours and hidden coves.The walk concludes in the charming fishing village of Rozel Bay, known for its colourful cottages and harbour. A popular tradition for many walkers is stopping at the Hungry Man Café on the pier for a breakfast roll or visiting the local tea rooms to enjoy fresh Jersey ice cream. For those using public transport, LibertyBus Route 3 serves Rozel, providing a convenient way to return to St Helier after your hike.
